tools.name: nmap
tools.notes: XML output parseable; standard first step in nearly all agents; service version detection via -sV flag

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.notes: Automated SQL injection discovery and exploitation; Python-based; output parseable but verbose

tools.name: Metasploit Framework
tools.notes: Interactive msfconsole requires tmux+prompt detection for autonomous use (Decepticon pattern); covers exploitation through post-exploitation

tools.name: BloodHound / SharpHound
tools.notes: Neo4j graph backend; outputs attack paths; requires domain credentials to run; results fed to lateral movement planning

tools.name: certipy
tools.notes: ADCS abuse: ESC1–ESC15 attack vectors; requires CA enumeration and template misconfiguration; Decepticon AD Operator agent

tools.name: mimikatz
tools.notes: Windows credential dumping; requires LSASS access; detected by modern AV/EDR; Decepticon Post-Exploit agent

tools.name: evil-winrm
tools.notes: WinRM interactive shell; requires valid credentials; tmux integration in Decepticon for prompt detection

tools.name: Nuclei
tools.notes: Template-based scanner; fast; covers CVE detection and exploit PoCs; YAML template library; output parseable

tools.name: gobuster / dirbuster
tools.notes: Wordlist-based directory brute forcing; PentestGPT context explosion documented (thousands of tokens per run)

tools.name: RustScan
tools.notes: Faster than nmap for initial port discovery; typically used before nmap for service detection; ARTEMIS pipeline

tools.name: NetExec (CrackMapExec)
tools.notes: SMB/LDAP/WinRM enumeration; 100% usage in cochise; pass-the-hash and credential spraying capable

tools.name: Impacket suite
tools.notes: 30+ Python scripts; GetUserSPNs (Kerberoasting), GetNPUsers (AS-REP roasting); cochise at 100%/83% usage respectively

tools.name: Hydra
tools.notes: Network protocol brute forcer; SSH, FTP, HTTP, SMB; VulnBot Exploitation phase

tools.name: hashcat / john
tools.notes: Offline hash cracking; hashcat GPU-accelerated; john CPU; cochise: hashcat 94% failure rate with auto-repair

tools.name: ffuf
tools.notes: Fast web fuzzer; directory and parameter fuzzing; output JSON-parseable; dominant tool in MAPTA per Figure 6

tools.name: Nikto
tools.notes: Web server vulnerability scanner; identifies misconfigurations and known CVEs; VulnBot Scanning phase

tools.name: WPScan
tools.notes: WordPress-specific vulnerability scanner; plugin/theme enumeration; VulnBot Scanning phase

tools.name: Chisel
tools.notes: TCP/UDP tunneling over HTTP; typically used for firewall bypass in post-exploitation; no agent confirmed to use autonomously

tools.name: Kubescape / kubectl
tools.notes: Kubernetes cluster security assessment; RBAC enumeration; misconfiguration discovery; Dark-Moon Kubernetes agent
